tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

1	// What the model is told in the printer panel: its system prompt. Written
     2	// here, on the page, and handed to the app with printer_instructions; the app
     3	// sends it with every request of the session and offers every printer tool
     4	// in every session. The facts it states -- the printer list, what is on the
     5	// network, the printer this is about -- come from the app in the session's
     6	// `context`.
     7	
     8	import type { PrinterSessionPayload } from './bridge/protocol';
     9	import { numberText, sizesText } from './printerWords';
    10	
    11	const CORE =
    12	  "You are JusPrin's printer assistant, talking to someone who may never have used a slicer. The goal is that their " +
    13	  'printer is set up so they can prepare prints for it, and connected over the network if that helps them and they want it.\n' +
    14	  'Use plain language, one to three short sentences. Ask one question at a time, and say where to find any answer you ask ' +
    15	  'for. Avoid internal terms such as profile, preset and catalog.\n' +
    16	  'When the person plainly states what to do or what changed ("I put a 0.6 nozzle on it", "yes, add it", "put it back ' +
    17	  'to 0.4"), do it: call the tool without asking again. When you are guessing -- which model from a photo or a vague ' +
    18	  'description, which printer on the network -- ask first and stop: that reply calls no ' +
    19	  'tool, and you act on the person\'s answer. ' +
    20	  'After a tool result, say what happened in the person\'s terms. Never say something is done before a tool says so. ' +
    21	  'Write every fact from the tools and the facts below, never from memory. Messages from the app (developer role) state ' +
    22	  'what happened; they are facts, not requests.\n' +
    23	  'Answers to tap: whenever your message asks a yes-or-no question, asks the person to confirm something, or asks ' +
    24	  'them to pick from a few options, its last line must be "Choices: first | second | third" -- two to four short ' +
    25	  'answers, each under 30 characters, written as the person would say them. The person taps one instead of typing, ' +
    26	  'and it reaches you as their own message. Leave the line out only when you need free text, such as an address or ' +
    27	  'a model name, and never write anything after it. Examples:\n' +
    28	  'From your photo, that looks like the Anycubic Kobra 3. Is that it?\nChoices: Yes, that is it | Different printer\n' +
    29	  'Which one is yours?\nChoices: Prusa MK4 | Prusa MK4S | Prusa MK4S HF\n' +
    30	  'Rules for finding the printer:\n' +
    31	  '- Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament first; the plate and filament are ' +
    32	  'chosen when preparing a print.\n' +
    33	  '- The person names one model plainly: call printer_identify with it, then add it with printer_add, with the nozzle ' +
    34	  'it ships with unless they said another. Then say which nozzle it was set up with and that you can change it if ' +
    35	  'theirs is different. One model fits a photo or a vague description: show it with printer_identify and ask if that ' +
    36	  'is it. ' +
    37	  'Two or three genuinely fit: call it with all of them and ask which, one choice each. More than three fit: do not ' +
    38	  'call it; ask one question that narrows it down, or offer to browse the full list (printer_manual_setup). Nothing ' +
    39	  "fits, or it isn't a filament printer: say so, offer the full list, and never offer a closest substitute.\n" +
    40	  '- A name that is the start of more than one model is not one model, even when it equals one of them: "prusa mk4" ' +
    41	  'begins Prusa MK4, MK4S and MK4S HF, so it is three printers.\n' +
    42	  '- A photo names a model only from a readable name or printed size; going by shape alone, ask for a photo of the ' +
    43	  'label. Never judge size from how big it looks. A clone uses the model it copies.\n' +
    44	  '- Pass a nozzle only when the person or a photo said its size, and never substitute a size they did not confirm. ' +
    45	  'After unknown_nozzle, name the sizes supported for that model and ask them to check the marking on the nozzle.\n' +
    46	  '- alreadyYours means settings for the same model were saved before, not that this machine was added.\n' +
    47	  'Rules for changing a printer:\n' +
    48	  '- Work out what physically changed and change only that with printer_change; afterwards say what that means ("Every ' +
    49	  'project that uses the K1 now slices for 0.6 mm."). If what changed is unclear, ask. Putting it back is the same tool.\n' +
    50	  "- The plate belongs to each project, not the printer. Nozzle material, such as hardened steel, isn't tracked.\n" +
    51	  '- A nozzle mismatch reported by the printer is something to offer to fix with printer_change.\n' +
    52	  'Rules for connecting a printer:\n' +
    53	  '- The connection tools act on the printer this is about, named below; a printer found on the network is only ever ' +
    54	  'a deviceId.\n' +
    55	  '- Connecting is optional; after adding, offer it once. For a Bambu Lab printer, call printer_connection_status and ' +
    56	  'connect to a printer it lists; with more than one, ask which. None listed means LAN mode is off or it is on another ' +
    57	  'network: say where to turn LAN mode on (on the printer\'s screen, in its network settings; ask what they see rather ' +
    58	  'than invent a menu). For Moonraker or OctoPrint, ask for the address they open it with in a browser, including its ' +
    59	  'port when there is one, then call printer_connect.\n' +
    60	  '- Never ask for a password, access code or API key in chat, and never repeat one: printer_connect shows a card where ' +
    61	  'the person types it. If printer_connect comes back cancelled, say at most a few words; if the person wrote a message ' +
    62	  'instead, answer that.\n' +
    63	  '- "connecting" means the app is still waiting for the printer: say you are checking, in one short line, and wait for ' +
    64	  "the app's note. A failure that is a timeout means no response, not a wrong code. After two failures, offer to enter " +
    65	  'the connection details themselves (printer_manual_connection).\n' +
    66	  '- Call printer_setup_finish only when the person says they are done, such as tapping Done; it closes this ' +
    67	  'conversation, so never call it on your own.\n';
    68	
    69	export function printerInstructions(session: PrinterSessionPayload): string {
    70	  const { context } = session;
    71	  let text = CORE;
    72	  if (session.mode === 'add') text += '\nThe person is adding a printer.\n';
    73	  if ((context.network ?? []).length > 0)
    74	    text += 'On the network now: ' + context.network!.map((found) => `${found.name} (${found.serial})`).join(', ') + '\n';
    75	  const printer = context.printer;
    76	  if (printer) {
    77	    text += `\nThe printer this is about:\nName: ${printer.name}\n`;
    78	    if (printer.model) text += `Brand and model: ${printer.model}\n`;
    79	    text += `Nozzle: ${printer.nozzle > 0 ? `${numberText(printer.nozzle)} mm` : 'unknown'}`;
    80	    if (printer.nozzles.length > 0) text += ` (this model ships ${sizesText(printer.nozzles)})`;
    81	    text += '\nSpools loaded:';
    82	    if (printer.spools.length === 0) text += ' none recorded';
    83	    for (const spool of printer.spools)
    84	      text += `\n- ${spool.name || spool.material} (${spool.material}${spool.colour ? `, ${spool.colour}` : ''})`;
    85	    text += `\nConnected to this app: ${printer.connected ? 'yes' : 'no'}\n`;
    86	    text += `Connects through: ${printer.provider === 'bambu' ? 'Bambu Lab LAN mode' : 'Moonraker or OctoPrint'}\n`;
    87	  }
    88	  if (context.printers) {
    89	    text += '\nPrinter list (catalogId | brand and model | build volume):\n';
    90	    for (const [id, name, volume] of context.printers) text += `${id} | ${name} | ${volume || '?'}\n`;
    91	  }
    92	  return text;
    93	}

No. The finding still holds on the current branch (`jusprin-newui` at bd8ea51abc). Nothing in the app posts a receipt or a "connect it?" offer when a printer is added. The model still writes that moment, and only a loose prompt rule guides it.

**What happens on a successful add**

- `PrinterConversation::add` ([PrinterConversation.cpp:401](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:401)) saves the printer, tells the host the printer list changed, and returns `{"printer": ...}` to the model. It adds no message, card or chip row to the conversation. By contrast, `printer_identify`, just above it, does push a block of printer cards.
- The only thing the app does itself is highlight the new printer's card on Home's printer list: a one-time CSS animation ([PrinterCard.tsx:21](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx:21), wired through [ShellController.cpp:254](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:254)). The printer panel fills the whole window, so I expect the person only sees that highlight after leaving the conversation. That is inference; I didn't run the app to confirm it.

**What the prompt says** ([printerInstructions.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts)). The line numbers in the finding still match this file.

- Line 33–35: after `printer_add`, "say which nozzle it was set up with and that you can change it if theirs is different."
- Line 55: "Connecting is optional; after adding, offer it once." It gives no wording and no chip labels. The general chip rule (lines 23–27) lets the model write its own labels, so bare "Yes / No" chips are allowed.

**Tests**

- The unit tests only check that the save happens and that a second add of the same model is refused.
- The live test, which runs the real model against a fake printer, doesn't count the offer. It opens the connect flow directly, and it only says "Yes, connect it" if the model hasn't already opened the card ([shell_harness.cpp:1052–1058](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:1052)). So a run where the model never offers to connect still passes.

The last commit to touch this area, 8334b3395b ("Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives"), removed Home's "printer added" strip. It didn't add anything in its place.

Both fixes the finding suggests are still open:
- **App-posted:** `add` pushes a fixed line and chip row, such as "Creality K1 is ready. Connect it over Wi-Fi?" with "Connect it" and "Not now".
- **Prompt-fixed:** the prompt names the exact wording and chips for this one moment, and a live check counts the offer over repeated runs.

I can start on either one.

8334b3395b Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives
The printer panel on Home was a three-phase flow with a different screen,
hard-coded buttons and one assistant tool per phase. It is now only a
conversation: the assistant adds, changes and connects printers through
eight tools, and every button the person taps is a reply the assistant
suggested ("Choices: a | b" as its last line, drawn as chips). The one card
left is printer_connect's, where an access code or API key is typed; it goes
straight to the connection and never into the conversation, the model's
requests, any note or the saved document.

- Tools: printer_identify, printer_add, printer_change,
  printer_connection_status, printer_connect, printer_manual_setup,
  printer_manual_connection, printer_setup_finish. Adding and changing run
  on the person's word: a new "confirmed in conversation" approval
  exemption, allowed only for printer panel tools. The connection tools act
  on the printer the conversation is about.
- The assistant acts on plain statements ("I put a 0.6 nozzle on it") and
  asks only when it is guessing; naming a model adds it with the nozzle it
  ships with. A second add of the same model in one conversation is refused.
- A message sent while the credential card waits cancels the card, so a
  question such as "where is the access code?" gets its answer.
- Bambu Lab LAN only: discovery starts once per session, a printer's name
  is accepted as its device id, and the outcome of a connection reaches the
  model as a note. Connecting a printer that was already selected no longer
  fails with "The selected printer changed": the backend deselects it and
  selects it again one event turn later, after GUI_App's lost-connection
  notice has run.
- The panel always takes the whole window: Back, a menu with OrcaSlicer's

a975c79be6 2026-09-20 Printer conversation panel: opener wording, photo previews, receipt lifetime, leave confirmation, dirty-state, and Bambu spool simulation
A batch of fixes to the printer conversation panel (the "Add printer" /
"Change printer" chat, and the Home screen it hands back to):

- The Add opener no longer promises anything about connecting; the
  Change opener drops the same promise. A network-found printer
  connects now, with Add, when it has one; a printer named from words
  or a photo has no such field, so connecting it isn't possible there.

- Attached photos render as a real thumbnail, at any original size --
  the old code only ever embedded the original file unchanged, and
  only when it was already under 256 KiB, so most real phone photos
  showed as a bare "IMAGE / filename" chip. Decoding needs wx, which
  the GUI-free agent-bridge test target does not link, so the decoder
  lives behind an injected seam (AgentHost::set_image_thumbnail_maker)
  the same way the existing MCP-CLI and reveal-path seams do.

- Home's "printer added" receipt now leads the column with the printer
  just added, names it plainly, and says what the card assumed rather
  than a bare signal. It shows immediately after a successful Add and
  clears on the very next unrelated state push -- fixed twice: once for
  the receipt's own logic, and again after live testing found the
  panel's own close sequence was sending a second, blank push a moment
  later that wiped the receipt before anyone could see it. The fix
  threads the added printer's facts through the deferred close itself
  instead of a separate call ahead of it, so there is only ever one
  push, not a race between two.

- Leaving the printer panel with something unsaved -- a draft still in
  the composer, a photo staged but not sent, an Add proposal on its
  card, or a Change still waiting on its own approval -- now asks
  first, rather than the old check (message count) which also caught
  an already-applied Change with nothing left to lose. Live testing
  found the panel's own composer never told the host what was typed,
  so the check read a value that was always stale; fixed by tracking
  the composer's live text on the page itself instead.

- The tool-only turn ("Looking through the printer list...", "Working
  on it...") names the right tool for Add vs Change instead of a
  hardcoded string that only happened to match one of them.

lastPrompt: What do you mean? Are you talking about hard coding the logics in the middle of the agent chat flow? If that's the case, how can we avoid the problems that we have done a lot of work to remove? Check…

content.text:
Yes. The first fix I relayed from the finding, where the app posts a fixed line and fixed buttons after a successful add, would hard-code the chat flow. That is the kind of scripting the recent commits removed. I shouldn't have offered it as the simple option.

**What the recent commits removed, and why**

- **8334b3395b** ("Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives") replaced a three-step flow. That flow had its own screens, hard-coded "Add" and "Not this one" buttons, a success screen with a "Connect printer" button, and a "printer added" banner on Home. Now every button the person taps is a reply the assistant suggested. The only fixed card left is the one where an access code is typed, so the code never enters the chat.
- **a975c79be6** shows what the "printer added" banner cost. Its lifetime had to be fixed twice, because a second, blank refresh from the panel closing wiped it before anyone saw it. The same commit also fixed a hard-coded "Working on it..." line that only matched one of the two tools.
- **4d4f9e466b** removed a fixed summary card pinned above the chat, and moved that guidance into what the assistant says.

**What a fixed receipt in the chat would bring back.** This is my reasoning, not something I tested:

- **Two voices in one thread.** The assistant writes its own reply after the add, then the app adds its line. The person could get two receipts, or two that disagree.
- **Wrong in some cases.** Something like "Connect it over Wi-Fi?" is wrong if the person already said "add it and connect it". It is also wrong when the connection is by address rather than Bambu's LAN mode.
- **Buttons the assistant didn't write.** Tapping "Connect it" arrives as the person's message, replying to a question the assistant never asked.
- **Timing bugs.** The line has to land in the right place relative to the assistant's reply, which is the same kind of race the old banner had.

**What I'd do instead.** Keep the assistant in charge, and make this one moment consistent through the prompt and a test:

1. In [printerInstructions.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts), replace "after adding, offer it once" (line 55) with a specific requirement. Every reply to a successful add says which printer and nozzle were saved, then offers to connect, with suggested replies the assistant writes, such as "Connect it | Not now".
2. Add a check to the live test that counts across repeated runs whether that offer appears. The nozzle rule was measured the same way. Today the test still passes when the offer is missing.

That keeps your decision that the assistant writes the chips. Do you want me to make that prompt change and add the live check?

content.text:
Yes. The chat already has a mechanism for exactly this, and it's how the printer candidate cards work today. One correction first: those cards no longer have an "Add this one" button. Commit 8334b3395b removed it. The person now answers the assistant's question, by tapping a suggested reply or typing, and the assistant calls `printer_add`.

**How the candidate cards work now**

1. When the assistant calls `printer_identify`, the app records a card entry in a list kept separately from the chat messages ([PrinterConversation.cpp:395](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:395)). Each entry has a kind (`"printers"`), the printers' names and pictures, and `afterMessageId`, the id of the chat message it follows.
2. The app sends that list to the chat page with the rest of the session state. The page draws each card right after its message ([MessageList.tsx:149](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx:149)). The type is defined in [protocol.ts:403](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:403), and its comment says no card has anything to tap.
3. **The list never reaches the model.** It is only read when the session state is sent to the page (line 268). The model learns what the cards show from the tool's own result, which carries the same printers as data.

So the cards are display-only and sit outside the model's history, which is what you're describing.

**A receipt built the same way**

- `PrinterConversation::add` adds an entry of a new kind, such as `"added"`, carrying the saved printer's name and nozzle. It uses the same code `identify` already uses.
- The page draws that kind as a receipt card.
- The model is unchanged: it still gets the `printer_add` result and writes its own reply.

I'd have the app create the card when the tool succeeds, not have the model write a tag like `<printer_added>` in its text. The app-created card appears only when the save really happened, in the same wording every time. A tag the model writes could be left out, misspelled, or written before the save succeeded. The page would also have to remove it from the text, and so would the chat history sent to the model.

**This avoids the earlier problems.** The receipt is a card, not a second chat message, so the thread still has one voice. Its buttons, if any, stay the assistant's. And its lifetime is the conversation's, not a separate refresh, which is how the old Home banner got wiped.

**What it doesn't fix:** the offer to connect. That is still the model's words, so it would still need the prompt change and the live test that counts it. The prompt should also tell the model the receipt card already shows what was saved, so it doesn't repeat it and just offers to connect.

Do you want me to build the receipt card this way?

content.text:
**The proposal:** when a printer is saved, show a small "printer added" card in the chat. The app draws it from the save itself, the AI never sees it, and the AI's text reply stays as it is.

**How it works**

- The chat window shows two kinds of things. There are chat messages, which are sent to the AI on every request. And there are display-only cards, which are stored in a separate list and never sent to the AI.
- The printer picture cards, the ones shown when the AI suggests which model you might have, are already display-only cards. Each card records which message it follows, and the chat window draws it there.
- I'd add one more card type, "printer added", with the printer's name and nozzle size. The app creates it in the same code that saves the printer, and only if the save succeeds.
- The chat window draws it as a receipt under the AI's reply.

**Why a card from the app, not a tag the AI writes:** the app knows for certain whether the save worked. If the AI wrote a tag like `<printer_added>`, it could forget it, get it wrong, or write it before the save actually happened. Every place that builds the AI's history would also have to strip it out.

**Why this doesn't bring back the old problems:** it isn't a scripted chat message. It has no buttons, and it doesn't change what the AI says or which reply suggestions it offers. It's a read-only card, like the picture cards already in the chat.

**What it doesn't solve:** whether the AI offers to connect the printer afterwards. That is still up to the AI. I'd handle it separately: tell the AI in its instructions that the card already shows what was saved, so it doesn't need to repeat it, and that it should always offer to connect next. Then add a test that runs the real AI several times and checks that the offer appears every time.

=== printer-live-harness-lessons.md
  modified: 2026-09-23T22:16:03.023Z
---

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].
=== screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture.md
  modified: 2026-09-23T21:16:58.377Z
---

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

=== agent-panel-css-namespaces.md
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
=== jusprin-worktree-build.md
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.
=== live-test-built-app-on-mac.md
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
=== background-bash-timeout-kills-builds.md
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

=== agent-panel-css-namespaces.md
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
=== jusprin-worktree-build.md
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.
=== live-test-built-app-on-mac.md
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
=== background-bash-timeout-kills-builds.md
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

  'chosen when preparing a print.\n' +
  '- The person names one model plainly: call printer_identify with it, then add it with printer_add, with the nozzle ' +
  'it ships with unless they said another. Then say that you can change the nozzle if theirs is different. One model ' +
  'fits a photo or a vague description: show it with printer_identify and ask if that ' +
  'is it. ' +
  'Two or three genuinely fit: call it with all of them and ask which, one choice each. More than three fit: do not ' +
  'call it; ask one question that narrows it down, or offer to browse the full list (printer_manual_setup). Nothing ' +
  "fits, or it isn't a filament printer: say so, offer the full list, and never offer a closest substitute.\n" +
  '- A name that is the start of more than one model is not one model, even when it equals one of them: "prusa mk4" ' +
  'begins Prusa MK4, MK4S and MK4S HF, so it is three printers.\n' +
  '- A photo names a model only from a readable name or printed size; going by shape alone, ask for a photo of the ' +

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
