input.prompt: In /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (branch jusprin-newui), `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` `--printer-live` mode can segfault. `live_send()` (around line 663) calls `live_panel()->host()->on_page_message(...)` without checking that `host()` is non-null. When the live model closes the printer panel early (seen 2026-09-23: after the scripted "the plate is smooth PEI now" the log printed "HARNESS LIVE   (the panel closed)", then the check live_plate_is_the_projects failed), the next scripted `say("i put a 0.3 on it")` dereferences a null host, and the harness exits with code 139 and no result line. Fix: make a step whose panel has closed fail with a named check (or reopen the session) instead of crashing, so a run always ends with a HARNESS RESULT line. Reproduce first per the repo's bug-fix policy: e.g. temporarily make a step close the panel (send the printer_setup_finish path, or call the panel's close) before a live_say step, and confirm the segfault. Then show the fixed behaviour. Build target: shell_integration_harness (`cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target shell_integration_harness jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`). The live mode needs OPENAI_API_KEY, and each run leaves a data dir holding the key at the path printed after "HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection:". Delete only the dir your own run printed.

name: printer-prompt-card-wording-breaks-connect
description: A printer-prompt line saying "the app shows a card" after printer_add broke the live connect step 0/3 vs 3/3; the "Printer added" receipt card shipped with the prompt unchanged
metadata:
  type: project
---

2026-09-23, jusprin-newui (uncommitted at the time): a "Printer added" receipt card was added. PrinterConversation::add pushes a display-only block of kind "added", and the page draws it; the model never sees it. I also tried adding a line to printerInstructions.ts: "Once printer_add succeeds, the app shows a card under your message... Do not announce the save again". Measured with --printer-live: with that line the connect step failed in 3 of 3 runs that reached it (the model invented a deviceId such as "<from_status>" and got unknown_device, and once told the person "I showed a card"). Without it, the connect step passed in 3 of 3. The line was dropped. Even with it, the model still said "Added." in 4 of 4 runs.

**Why:** the prompt already calls printer_connect's credential entry "a card". A second, app-drawn "card" seems to blur which card the model controls. That cause is my hypothesis, not proven; the pass/fail split was measured.

**How to apply:** any prompt wording about the receipt needs a live A/B across at least 3 runs per arm. Avoid the word "card" for anything except printer_connect's. Full --printer-live runs flake on their own (the full-list step and the connect step each failed in some runs of both arms), so compare arms rather than trusting one run. See [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

content.text:
The printer setup chat now shows a "Printer added" card when a printer is saved. It shows the printer's name and nozzle size, and the AI never sees it. It appeared correctly in every test run, including 7 runs against the real AI. One gap is left: the AI's own reply still says the printer was added, so the save is stated twice. My attempt to stop that broke the connect step, so I took it back out. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works**
- When `printer_add` saves a printer, `PrinterConversation::add` records a display-only card, the same way the printer picture cards are recorded. The card goes under the chat message that asked for the save. If the save fails, or the same model is added again in one conversation, no card is added.
- The chat page draws it as a green check with "Printer added", then the name and nozzle, for example "Creality K1 · 0.4 mm nozzle". It has no buttons.
- The AI's instructions are unchanged.

I've attached screenshots in light and dark: naming a model, choosing one of three by tapping a suggested reply, and a long name in a narrow window. The narrow-window case showed a real problem: the long name cut the nozzle size off behind "…". I fixed it so the line wraps.

**Checks**

Not in a way that would really expose the problem. The failure is a choice the live AI makes: with that line in the system prompt, it made up a printer id. Unit tests here don't call the AI. They use a scripted fake that gives the same answer whatever the prompt says, so no unit test can show that one prompt makes the AI behave worse than another.

Two things are possible:

1. **A unit test on the prompt text.** It would fail if the prompt ever calls anything a "card" other than the access-code card that connecting opens. It is fast, needs no AI, and would have caught my line. The catch: it encodes my guess about why connect broke, which I haven't proven. It could flag wording that is fine, or miss wording that breaks connect some other way.

2. **A repeated live test.** It runs just the connect conversation against the real AI five to ten times and reports how often the AI passes a printer id the app refuses. This is the check that actually exposes the problem: it failed 3 of 3 with my line and passed 3 of 3 without it. It costs API calls, takes a few minutes, and its result is a rate, not a pass or fail.

I'd build the second, since it measures the real behaviour, and add the first only if you want a cheap guard in the regular tests. Which do you want?
